site.author: Angela St. Cyr
site.about_short: Angela St. Cyr is a home stylist, blogger, and enthusiastic cook based in Vancouver, Canada — one of the most expensive cities in North America. With her two daughters now grown and out in the world of their own, Angela continues to prove that you can live and design the life you want, regardless of budget. Home Stylist, Blogger, Enthusiastic Cook, former participant in the 100-Mile Challenge, and a longtime Jamie Oliver Food Revolution Ambassador.

recipes.title: Sticky Chile Lime Chicken Salad
recipes.description: Sweet, salty, and just enough heat to make your tastebuds hum.

sections.text: I LOVE salads!!! It doesn't matter what time of year, give me an interesting salad with a bold mix of flavours and I'm in! This is one of my all time favourites, it's sweet and salty with just enough heat to get your tastebuds humming. This recipe generously serves 4, allowing for 2 chicken thighs per person.
For the chicken & marinade

items: 8 boneless chicken thighs (skin on or off)
1/4 cup olive oil (lime-infused if you can find it)
Pop everything except the chicken into a blender or food processor and pulse until it becomes a smooth sauce.
Remove 1/4 cup of the sauce and set aside — this will be the base for the salad dressing.
Pour the remaining sauce over the chicken and marinate for at least an hour, or up to overnight.

sections.text: For the salad
While the chicken is marinating, prepare your salad. This is what I like to use, but feel free to swap in anything that suits your taste:
For the dressing

items: 1 tbsp sweet chile sauce (I like Aroy-D)
Whisk everything together in a small bowl.
Season with salt and pepper if needed.
Feel free to add a little more oil or rice vinegar to balance the acidity to your taste.

sections.text: To cook the chicken

items: Remove the chicken from the marinade and cook either in a non-stick skillet or on the barbecue.
Sear one side of the chicken for about 5 minutes.
Flip it over and drizzle 1 tsp of sweet chile sauce over the seared side of each piece.
Cook the other side for 5 minutes, then flip again and drizzle another teaspoon of chile sauce over the second side.
Cook for another few minutes per side until the sauce is sticky and the chicken reads 165°F (75°C) on a meat thermometer.

sections.text: Place the cooked, sliced chicken onto the prepared salad and drizzle with the dressing. This is guaranteed to become a family favourite!
One of my fave easy, healthy breakfasts.

recipes.title: Roasted Butternut Squash Soup
recipes.description: FOOD This soup just screams fall don't you think?

sections.text: FOOD This soup just screams fall don't you think? It's rich, creamy and hearty enough to keep you satisfied and warm all day. Best of all, this soup gets better and better as it sits so it's the perfect make ahead meal if you've got a busy week.
salt and pepper to taste

items: Cut the squash in half and scoop out the seeds. Sprinkle with salt and pepper and drizzle with olive oil. Place it on a parchment lined cookie sheet cut side down and bake for 45 minutes or until fork tender. Once the squash is soft, remove from the oven and let cool.

Now all I do is scoop out half of the cooked squash and put it in the blender with the onion, garlic, rosemary and half of the chicken stock. Give it a whiz. Once it's silky smooth I pour it into a medium sized pot on medium low heat. Repeat with the remaining squash and stock.
Once all your pureed squash is in the pot simply stir in the wine and simmer for at least 20 minutes or you can simmer it on low heat for several hours if you'd like.
Turn the heat off and just before serving stir in the remaining ingredients. Season with salt pepper and nutmeg.

recipes.tip:
You could easily pop this into a crock pot on low and just let it simmer away all day. Just remember don't stir in the butter and cream until just before serving.

 This can easily be made vegan by simply swapping out the butter with a vegan butter like Earth Balance and using a bouillon cube like Edward & Sons Not- Chick'n

recipes.title: The Perfect Yorkshires Every Time
recipes.description: I'm not English so I'm not going to pretend that making Yorkshire Puddings is second nature to me, but I will share with you the few tricks I've learned after many years of making some pretty sub-par Yorkshires.

sections.text: I could never understand why sometimes they would turn out like rubbery hockey pucks and other times they'd be as close to perfect as you can get when I was always using the same recipe. So over the years I've researched all the tricks that people swore by and with a little experimenting of my own I've come up with a fool proof method for making these finicky little puffs of heaven.

items: First off you MUST use very good quality free range eggs. I've tried them with regular grocery store eggs a thousand times and I'm never able to get consistent results. I suppose happy chickens make better quality eggs, so I'm more than willing to pay the extra price for them. Always make sure your eggs are room temperature before making this recipe.

My second tip is ALWAYS use full fat milk, I'm assuming there is something in the extra fat of the milk that helps these baby's fluff up to epic heights while still allowing them to be light and crisp.

Another tip is to whiz everything up in your blender. The more air you can get into your batter the better. I give them a good whiz to combine all the ingredients thoroughly, let it sit for about 10 minutes or so and then give them another good whiz.

Now you're going to hate this tip but let the mixture sit in the fridge overnight or for at least a few hours. This seems to be key for consistently perfect Yorkies. Be sure to bring back to room temperature before cooking and give the mixture another whiz in your blender before filling your tins.

For my last tip... be sure to get your shortening or pan drippings piping hot before you pour your batter into your tins. You should hear it sizzle as you pour in the batter. If it doesn't sizzle put your tins back in the oven for a little longer.

sections.text: Now that you have all my tips, here's my recipe

items: Follow all the tips above...don't skip a single one!
Preheat oven to 475 degrees once your batter has come back to room temperature.

Drop 1/2 tsp of shortening or pan drippings into each muffin tin... I like to use shortening because it has a very high smoke point and the Yorkshires stay a pretty golden colour. Place the muffin tin in the oven until the shortening is melted and smoking hot. This usually takes at least 5 minutes.

Now pour enough batter to fill each tin to 3/4. Pop the tins back in the oven and cook for 15-20 minutes. DO NOT OPEN THE DOOR AT ALL DURING THIS TIME. Turn your oven light on after 15 minutes and check to see if they are risen and perfectly browned. If not leave them alone for another 5 minutes.
That's it. If you follow each of these steps you'll have perfect Yorkshires every time!

recipes.title: MUFFIN OF THE MONTH - Strawberry Rhubarb Crumble
recipes.description: It finally feels like spring!!! Any of you living in Vancouver will understand the joy I'm feeling at this moment. It's been a long grey, wet, cold winter and frankly I'm thrilled to see it come to an end.

sections.text: This months MUFFIN OF THE MONTH is a celebration of all things spring. I can't help myself, I always get a little excited when I see local rhubarb and strawberries at the market! It's a sure sign that warmer weather is finally on it's way. Go ahead and give these a try...they are a little taste of the sunshine that will soon be here to stay.
*see rhubarb tip below
grating of fresh nutmeg
Crumble Topping-

items: Toss everything together and give it a good stir. Set aside until you've filled your muffin cups.

sections.text: Preheat oven to 375 degrees.

In a large bowl combine the dry ingredients and stir in the diced rhubarb and strawberries. In a separate bowl beat the eggs until frothy, then add the remaining wet ingredients. Add the wet ingredients to the dry and stir just enough to moisten. Too much mixing makes a tuff muffin. Fill lined muffin cups 3/4 full (I use a large icecream scoop)

items: *If for some reason your muffin mix seems a little dry and stiff feel free to stir in a splash more liquid. Conversley if it ends up a little wet, add a sprinkle more flour. We've always been told baking is an exact science and for many recipes it is, but...I'll never post a recipe like that! All my recipes allow room for a little creative licence and a few corrective measures. So forget what momma always told you lol!
Now simply sprinkle an even portion of crumb topping on each muffin and then pop them in the oven for for 20-25 minutes or until slightly golden.

recipes.tip:
This recipe is easily made gluten free by simply swapping out the flour with a gluten free version such as Robin Hood or my favourite flour blend. You can also make this vegan easily by using an egg replacer.

If you prefer your rhubarb less tart simply sprinkle the diced rhubarb with some sugar and let it sit for a few minutes before adding it into the dry mix.

recipes.title: MUFFIN OF THE MONTH- Marshmallow Hot Chocolate
recipes.description: Well it's December and I'm feeling festive and perhaps a little naughty. Don't tell Santa!

sections.text: Normally my muffins are very healthy, they tend to have little to no added fat, low sugar...bla bla bla. Not this time my friends, it's Christmas so I'm going all out. Fat, sugar and all things yummy! No, these aren't cupcakes, they're still muffins with all their dense moist yumminess, but they are a treat so PLEASE don't eat these every morning for breakfast even though you may want to lol. Merry Christmas everyone. xox
(or 5 packets)

items: * You'll notice I haven't added any sugar. No, it's not a typo...I found the Hot chocolate powder had just the right amount so I decided to delete it.

Line your muffin tins with tulip muffin cups about 3/4 full (I use a large icecream scoop) when the muffins have about 2 or 3 minutes left carefully place a few mini-marshmallows on each muffin. recipes.title: Chocolate Pecan Pie

sections.text: This is probably my families favourite dessert! Toasting the pecans prior to baking the pie adds such richness and depth while helping to cut the sweetness of the chocolate. My daughter used to HATE pecan pie because she didn't like the jelly-like filling that formed around the pecans. The chocolate cuts down on that immensely, so now she loves Pecan Pie...well mine at least lol. If you try only one pie recipe in your life, this should be it!
Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
For the crust

items: 1/3c cold butter or shortening cut into cubes
TIP- If you use half butter and half shortening you'll get the perfect flakiness while still being tender and full of buttery flavour. It's a little more work but it's worth the effort in my opinion.
Pop everything except the water into the bowl of  your stand mixer. Mix on medium speed until the butter pieces are the size of small peas.

Now add 2tbsp of the cold water over the flour mixture and turn the mixer on low speed for a second. If all the flour is moistened and the pastry leaves the side of the bowl then you are finished. It's very important not to over-mix at this point or your crust will be tough. If your pastry isn't coming together yet add another tablespoon or so of water to the mixture and give it another stir. Take a bit of the pastry out and squeeze it. ...if it holds together it's ready, if not add a tiny bit more water and give it a gentle stir.

sections.text: Remove the dough from the mixer, knead it a couple of times and shape it into a flattened round and wrap in plastic wrap. Allow it to chill in the fridge for about 30 minutes. This will make it easier to work with.

items: Remove the dough from the fridge and unwrap it. Place the dough on a lightly floured surface. Using a rolling pin roll the pastry into a circle that's about 2" larger than your pie plate.
Fold the pastry into fourths and place in the pie plate. Unfold the dough and shift into place. Trim any excess pastry so it's 1" bigger than the rim of the pie plate.
Fold and roll the edge of the pastry under and flute the edges simply by pinching with your fingers. Prick the crust all over with a fork, it will help the steam escape while baking.
Set aside until the filling is ready.

sections.text: Filling

items: 1c Rogers Golden syrup or corn syrup
Pop everything except the pecans and the chocolate chips into a large bowl and give it a good whisk. Now stir in the toasted pecans and the chocolate chips.
Pour the filling into your prepared pie crust and cover the edge with a 3" strip of foil to prevent excess browning.

Bake for approximately one hour minutes, removing the foil for the last 15 minutes. You'll know it's ready when it looks all puffy and no longer seems liquid when you give the pan a wiggle. Remove from oven and let it cool for at least  an hour before serving.
I like to serve this with a dollop of vanilla whipped cream. Enjoy!

recipes.tip: I toast my pecans in the oven as soon as it's preheated... just until they become fragrant. It usually takes about 10 minutes or so.

recipes.title: Banana Bread
recipes.description: This is one of my family’s faves! Quick, easy and so delicious.

sections.text: Water

items: **The amount of water you need is dependent on the size and ripeness of your bananas so rather than having a set amount of water I add just enough water to make a thick batter.
This recipe couldn’t be easier! Simply pop all the dry ingredients into a large mixing bowl and give it a whisk.
Then add the wet ingredients and add a splash of water. Give everything a good stir… if it’s too thick add more water, if it’s the consistency of a thick cake batter then you’re  done.
Pour the mixture into a greased loaf pan and bake at 350 degrees F for about an hour or until a toothpick come out clean.
Let cool in the pan for about 15 minutes before tipping it out onto a cooling rack.

sections.text: Enjoy!

recipes.tip: I pop my whole peeled bananas into a ziplock bag then toss all the other wet ingredients into it. Squish it all up until the banana is mashed and the eggs are incorporated. Then I simply squeeze it into my dry ingredients and give it a good stir. Adjust the water as needed. Easy peasy!

recipes.title: Sushi...kind of
recipes.description: In the mood for sushi, but maybe you don't want to spend money eating out? Or perhaps you don't like all the mess when making it yourself? Well I have the best recipe ever!!!!

sections.text: I started making this at home when we used to have Korean home-stay children living with us. It's quick, easy, inexpensive and if I do say so myself, really delicious. All you need is a few packs of roasted seaweed (I get them at my produce market) some sticky rice...or even regular rice that you cook with too much water so it goes sticky. Who would of thought there was a use for improperly cooked rice LOL! Just a few other ingredients and you're done. Quick and easy homemade sushi...who would have thought? See the full recipe below:
several packs                 roasted seaweed

items: Set the seaweed and rice aside.
Mix all the other ingredients together in a bowl and stir.

To serve just let everyone make their own sushi rolls. Simply pick up a sheet of seaweed, add a spoonful of rice, then some tuna and fold in half like a taco. That's it just keep eating them as you make them. It's really a fun social way to eat... my kids love these when they have friends over!

items: Assemble as in the featured picture. If your calories and nutrients allow, feel free to add a second egg. This is one of my FAVOURITE breakfasts!
Get a large pot of water and bring it to a boil, this will be for cooking the noodles.

Now in a small pot pop in the next 10 ingredients and cook covered over medium heat for about 10 minutes or until the chicken thigh is fully cooked. Turn off the heat, remove the chicken breast and dice it up into a similar size as your vegetables and then return it to the pot.

By now the water for the noodles should be boiling so throw the noodles into the pot and cook according to package directions. Once cooked drain them and rinse well with fresh warm water and return the rinsed drained noodles to the pot.
At this point toss the snap peas and the frozen peas into the warm broth mixture and give it a stir. This allows the peas to slightly cook while staying bright green and crisp.
Pour the broth mixture on top of the prepared rice noodles and stir well to combine.
Garnish with thinly sliced green onions and sesame seeds.

This dish it fantastic warm, but dare I say it’s even better cold! So it’s the perfect make ahead recipe…have it fresh for dinner and then eat it cold as a quick and easy lunch. I eat a single serving for my meal but my husband eats a double quantity and then adjusts his carb intake accordingly for the rest of his meals.

sections.text: I’ve been using the MYFITNESSPAL app for some time now and was only getting pretty depressing results because  my weight was going up and down like a yo-yo. I had only been paying attention the the calories portion and assumed this less than stellar weight loss was because of my age and my inability to do any cardio other than slow walking. At my daughters insistence last week, I started concentrating on the Macros, Nutrients and the Calories portion of the app and I can’t believe the difference…I lost 5.9lbs in one week!!!!!!! I have 28lbs to loose so that’s a phenomenal start and it was substantial enough to keep me encouraged and wanting to learn new recipes and meal plans to keep me on track. I realize most people find this too time consuming in addition to the rest of the things they have to fit into their busy daily routines but I  ABSOLUTELY LOVE doing this kind of thing. So I thought it would be helpful to share my recipes and meal plans with those of you that either don’t have to time or don’t enjoy doing this sort of thing. We all have our strengths so there is no judgement on my part…I’m thrilled to be able to share this with all of you.

items: This recipe is the first MYFITNESSPAL inspired recipe I’ve added to my website, so this section will grow organically over time. I’ll also be sure to share my weight-loss successes and failures with you along the way. It feels so strange for me to be writing about an eating plan to help you loose weight because I absolutely abhor fad diets. I especially hate hearing people talk about them! In all fairness though this is the first time I’ve ever had to actively try to loose weight and it isn’t easy!!!! I’ve always been relatively the same weight and have been very balanced in my eating habits and the amount of daily exercise I get so I’ve never really had to think about it before…not even after I had kids! I left the hospital wearing the clothes I wore before I got pregnant. Feel free to roll your eyes lol.

sections.text: You’re probably thinking what the hell happened all of a sudden that started tipping the scale in the wrong direction! Well I got sick…VERY sick! Long story short I took an antibiotic that has a very rare side effect called Intra Cranial Hypertention which is your body producing too much cerebral spinal fluid which then puts pressure on your brain. The symptoms mimic those of a brain tumour which was VERY scary especially because I have 2 very dear friends that passed away from having brain tumours. After every test known to man and almost a year of seeing several specialists they are 99% sure that is what has happened…it will be confirmed in April after a lumbar puncture…insert scared face here 😳

items: On top of the hell that I’ve been through it’s also had the added bonus of me not being able to exercise or exert myself at all…for several months I could barely even get off the sofa without my brain feeling like it was going to explode. I went from consistently walking between 15,000-20,000 steps a day to 200 steps a day for a 3 month period and now have been able to gradually increase since then. I’m mostly better now but I still can’t do any type of cardio except slow walking, anything more and my head pressure starts up again and I’m out of commission for days.
So that’s my story in a nutshell, feel free to share your stories, weight-loss successes and struggles in the comment section…it’s always nice to feel like we aren’t alone in this.

recipes.title: Dark Chocolate Lava Cake in Less Than 5 Minutes
recipes.description: What’s a girl to do when she’s craving dessert but doesn’t have anything sweet in the house? And to make matters worse I have one kid that’s gluten intolerant and another that can’t have dairy!

sections.text: Well, they say necessity is the mother of invention and this recipe was created because of exactly that lol. This literally takes me less than five minutes to make from start to finish and I can either make it as a single serving by dividing the recipe by four or I can make 4 servings using the recipe as is and it still only takes 5 minutes…including cooking time! This recipe can be made either gluten free, dairy free or both if necessary. If you don’t have any allergies to consider…go ahead and make this with regular flour and dairy. This really is THE best dessert recipe for a tricky crowd. Are you ready? Here we go….

items: If you’re making this gluten free use a gluten free flour blend, Robin Hood makes a pretty good one and it’s easy to use because it’s already pre-blended. For a dairy free version use a dairy free milk, really any you have on hand will work well in this recipe. Also make sure the chocolate you use is dairy free as well.
Simply mix the dry ingredients together in a bowl and give a quick whisk. Now stir in the wet ingredients and mix until well combined and lump free. Divide equal portions into 4 mason jars or mugs.

Now press a square of chocolate into the centre of each mason jar and then microwave on high for a minute or two. Each microwave is different so keep an eye on it. You want the outside of the cake to look cooked but the centre still to be a bit runny, it will firm up slightly as it cools.
I like to serve this with a scoop of ice cream, some chocolate or caramel drizzle…or both lol…and a few toasted nuts.

sections.text: Enjoy!

* I have to put a little thank you here acknowledging the lovely Miss Tori. It was her that introduced me to the wonders of lava cake cooked in the microwave and she changed my life in an instant lol. My recipe is quite different than the one I tried at her house…in order to accommodate for allergies, but if it wasn’t for her I would never have come up with this. So thank you Tori ❤️

recipes.title: Hummus MYFITNESSPAL.com
recipes.description: This is a staple in our house... there is rarely a time when I don't have a fresh batch of Hummus in my fridge.

sections.text: Yes, you can buy pre-made Hummus virtually everywhere these days but you certainly can't beat homemade, especially made my way! I use very little oil and some of the chick pea water to make this Hummus lower in fat and silky smooth. I also have a few other little tricks that add such depth of flavour that this Hummus will be unlike any you've tried before!

items: Drain the chick peas but reserve the liquid. Now pop all the ingredients except the chickpea liquid into your food processor. Turn on your food processor and add just enough of the chickpea water to get it easily moving. It should be the consistency of loose natural peanut butter. Once you have the correct consistency continue to blend until it becomes silky smooth. Feel free to adjust the seasoning at this point, sometimes it needs a little more lemon or even a pinch more salt.

If you'd like to add a little more depth of flavour to your Hummus, why not try adding 1/4tsp cumin or stir in some finely chopped roasted red peppers. You can even make it a little spicy by adding some diced smokey chipotle peppers or a little of the dried powder. There are really endless possibilities to make this your own.
I serve it with a drizzle of olive or sesame oil and a sprinkling of toasted sesame seeds. This stores well in the fridge for at least a week. Enjoy!

recipes.title: Passion Tea Lemonade

items: Simply add the 4 teabags to the boing water and steep until the water is room temperature. Remove tea bags and stir in lemonade powder. Refrigerate until cold.
If you mix this with some vodka or gin it make an amazing martini!

recipes.tip: Instead of the lemon-aid powder you can use the juice of 4 lemons and sugar to taste.

recipes.title: Smokey Maple Whiskey Barbeque Sauce
recipes.description: Well it's FINALLY arrived...barbecue season is here!

sections.text: So to kick off this joyous occasion I thought I'd share my families’ fave barbecue sauce recipe. It's bold, rich and smokey with a slightly sweet sticky tang. Fantastic on chicken and ribs, even better mixed into hamburger meat before you form your patties...simply finger licking good.
Makes about 7 cups of sauce.

items: Toss it all in a large pot and simmer for a few hours. You can also make this in a crock pot on low if you have one, just toss everything in and forget about it until the next morning.

recipes.tip: I sometimes double this recipe, it keeps in the fridge for a very long time.

recipes.title: MUFFIN OF THE MONTH- Nutella Banana
recipes.description: Okay, I've died and gone to heaven! Why hadn't I thought of this before?!!!

sections.text: I love all things Nutella so being that I'm the muffin queen you'd think I would have been making these for years now...but sadly I haven't lol. I ran out of chocolate chips one day and the only other chocolate I had on hand was Nutella so a new and wonderful muffin was born and I've been making them ever since. If you're a fan of Nutella you're going to LOVE these!!!!
NUTELLA- see directions
Preheat oven to 375.

items: In a large bowl combine the dry ingredients. In a separate bowl beat the eggs until frothy, then add the remaining wet ingredients. Add the wet ingredients to the dry and stir just enough to moisten. Too much mixing makes a tuff muffin.

*If for some reason your muffin mix seems a little dry and stiff feel free to stir in a splash more liquid. Conversley if it ends up a little wet, add a sprinkle more flour. We've always been told baking is an exact science and for many recipes it is, but...I'll never post a recipe like that! All my recipes allow room for a little creative licence and a few corrective measures. So forget what momma always told you lol!

Take a few heaping tablespoons of Nutella and drop them onto your mixed batter. Now simply swirl it into the batter so it's relatively evenly distributed but you can still see distinct ribbons of Nutella running through the batter.
Fill lined muffin cups 3/4 full (I use a large icecream scoop) and place a dollop of Nutella in the centre of each muffin.
Bake for 20-25 minutes or until slightly golden.

recipes.tip: This recipe is easily made gluten free by simply swapping out the flour with a gluten free version such as Robin Hood or my favourite flour blend. You can also make this vegan easily by using an egg replacer and dairy free Nutella...YES that actually exists lol!!!! YAY!

recipes.title: Muffin Of The Month- Orange Cranberry

sections.text: I  absolutely LOVE anything orange flavoured, so I make these muffins quite regularly especially in the winter when our immune systems can sure benefit from a hit of vitamin C. Give them a go... they're easy peasy!

items: 1 295 ml container of frozen orange juice (thawed)

sections.text: Preheat oven to 375.

items: In a large bowl combine the dry ingredients. In a separate bowl beat the eggs until frothy, then add the remaining wet ingredients. Add the wet ingredients to the dry and stir just enough to moisten. Too much mixing makes a tuff muffin. *If for some reason your muffin mix seems a little dry and stiff feel free to stir in a splash more liquid. Conversley if it ends up a little wet, add a sprinkle more flour. All my recipes allow room for a little creative licence and a few corrective measures. So forget what momma always told you lol!

- This recipe is easily made gluten free by simply swapping out the flour with a gluten free version such as Robin Hood or my favourite flour blend. You can also make this vegan easily by using an egg replacer and vegan butter or simply replace the butter with coconut or vegetable oil. Nut milks and soy milk also work perfectly in this recipe.

recipes.tip: If I happen to have crystalline sugar in the house I'll sprinkle a bit on the of the muffins before baking. They really look quite pretty that way!

recipes.title: Asparagus Prosciutto Roses with Lemon Olive Oil
recipes.description: These look very intricate and complicated but I promise you with only two steps, they are as easy as can be!

sections.text: If you are lucky enough to have one of those lovely olive oil stores close to you, you can even skip step one and just purchase lemon olive oil. Makes six roses.
Step one

items: Pop both the lemon rind and the olive oil in a small saucepan on low heat for about 15 minutes or until you can smell the lemon. Remove the lemon rind and set aside to cool.

sections.text: Step 2

items: Place an asparagus spear on the plate.

Now fold a piece of prosciutto in half and roll it until it looks like a rose and is the size you want. Pinch one side...like making a tissue paper flower and cut off any excess length be sure to leave about  1” of the pinched bottom so your rose doesn't unravel. Reserve the bits you trimmed off for later use.
Place your rose on top of the pointy part of the asparagus, and voila you have a long stemmed rose!
Garnish with a few drops of olive oil, maybe even some lemon syrup and some chopped candied lemon if you have any. Repeat the process until you’ve completed all six.

sections.text: Anyone that knows me well knows that I'm a very frugal person. So when I ran out of my face cream I couldn't bare the thought of purchasing another jar of expensive cream... especially because I was wanting to replace it with something all natural that was free of any chemicals. "Natural" face regimes are all the rage right now as they should be, but because of the demand the prices are insanely high! Unacceptably high in my opinion. Everyone should be able to look and feel their best regardless of income level don't you think? So what's frugal girl to do? Well I looked to my pantry for some help lol. I figured if it's pure enough to ingest it's definitely pure enough to put on my skin, so I started to do a little research on different oils. I've used coconut oil on my body for years, but found it too greasy for my face and it clogged my pores which made me break out. I had tried olive oil in the past and it was an amazing moisturizer for my body but I couldn't stand the smell. I'd recently purchased avocado oil to use on salads but had never tried it as a moisturizer before so I figured what did I have to loose? Well, did I ever hit the JACKPOT!!!!!

items: Through my research I  discovered avocado oil is one of the richest sources of monounsaturated fatty acids which has an immediate effect on the texture and appearance of your skin. It's extremely good at hydrating and softening your skin and is also an effective treatment for acne,  blackheads, eczema and other types of skin inflammation. Some people even claim it helps to diminish age spots!

I've been using avocado oil for a little over two months now and I couldn't be happier with the results! I've been applying it both at night and in the morning right after I shower. The pores on my nose and chin are visibly reduced and my fine lines and wrinkles have noticeably lessened, so needless to say this is all I'm using from now on. I apply it just like you would an expensive face cream, using it very sparingly. A little goes a long way. The only major difference is you have to give it few few minutes to absorb. If after a few minutes it still seems a little greasy just simply wipe off the excess with a clean cloth and be sure to use even less the next time you apply it.

An added bonus I discovered completely by accident is, if I apply my foundation just before it's completely absorbed, it gives my skin a beautiful slightly dewy finish that makes my skin look like its absolutely glowing and dare I say youthful. I can't believe how many compliments I've been getting on my skin lately. I've always struggled with my skin, I've had hormonal cystic acne since I was a teenager, so needless to say, compliments on my skin are not something I'm used to!

Keeping things simple but also keeping things pretty has always been important to me so an ugly bottle of avocado oil sitting on my tiny bathroom counter was not working for me. So I bought a pretty little soap pump bottle for a couple of bucks, filled it with the avocado oil and placed it on the black lacquer tray I had sitting on the back of my toilet tank. Ugly problem solved and it's super convenient which means I use it regularly because I'm not always having to pull it in and out of the cupboard.
Check out the recipe for my FLOWER WATER TONER/ MAKE-UP REMOVER.
Avocado oil in my books... is a BEAUTIFUL THING!

recipes.title: Flower Water Toner/ Make-up Remover
recipes.description: I'm always looking for inexpensive natural alternatives for my skin care regime and I've come up with a few gems over the years.

sections.text: This one, I have to say is definitely one of my favourites. I simply combine equal parts Rose Flower Water and Orange Blossom Water that I buy at the grocery store or at an Indian or Persian market...if you're lucky enough to have one in your neighbourhood. They'll often sell it at a fraction of the cost because it's a common ingredient in their households both for cooking and for beauty purposes. Buying food grade flower waters ensures they are free of chemicals, my motto is if it's not safe enough to eat I don't want it on my skin either! Most commercially made toners are very expensive and are usually packed with chemicals and alcohol which can cause your skin dry out and sometimes even make your skin flake and peel.  This toner is a soft natural alternative, with some pretty impressive benefits due its naturally occurring vitamin content, and it costs me less than $8 to make enough to last me a year.

items: Flower waters have been used throughout history to help beautify your skin... even Cleopatra used them!  It's good for all skin types, from dry to oily and even combination skin. I don't know how it does it but it seems to just keep everything in perfect balance, likly due to its high content of vitamins A and C which are both very effective at helping to slough off dead skin cells without the use of anything abrasive which can often be too harsh on your skin. This flower water combination also has anti-inflammatory and an antiseptic properties so it's brilliant at keeping bacteria at bay which helps keep your pores clear and staves off acne break outs.

As if that wasn't enough it's also very effective at moisturizing your skin which will help it be more elastic. Any of you over 30 will recognize how important that is. How does it manage to achieve all of this in a simple flower water combination? It's because of the naturally occurring vitamins E, A and C. It will even help soothe a sunburn.

I apply it to may face with a cotton pad morning and night after washing my face. It works as a toner and helps lock in moisture which keeps your skin looking dewy and youthful. It's smells absolutely beautiful too, my husband comments on it every night when I slip into bed lol.

Another use for this little bottle of miracle water is as a make-up remover. Simply wet a cotton pad with it and your make-up will wipe off like a dream. If you have particularly difficult to remove water-proof mascara just wipe a little coconut oil over your lashes first and then use your dampened cotton pad. Removing mascara has never been easier!

I  store my flower water in a pretty little soap pump bottle and placed it on the black lacquer tray I had sitting on the back of my toilet tank. It's super convenient which means I use it regularly because I'm not always having to pull it in and out of the cupboard.
Check out the recipe for my SKIN FOOD moisturizing oil.
Flower Water is a beautiful thing!

recipes.title: MUFFIN OF THE MONTH- Carrot Cake
recipes.description: It's February and most of us are finished being overly restrictive on our "eat clean and stay fit" resolution for the New Year.

sections.text: We're now ready to be a little more realistic about what long term healthy eating should look like. So the MUFFIN OF THE MONTH this time is full of healthy ingredients but it will make you feel like you're having dessert for breakfast. Don't we all deserve that once in a while? Feeling like we get to eat a treat now and then really helps us stay on track for the long term, rather than the unrealistic "perfect eating" we all strive for but undoubtedly can never manage to achieve. These muffins have the decadence of a rich piece of carrot cake, they are  unbelievably moist but have far less fat and sugar than your average carrot cake recipe and really less than your average muffin too. So go ahead and give yourself a little treat for breakfast! It's almost guilt free...especially if you skip the icing or just use the tiniest dollop, just enough to satisfy your sweet tooth lol.
Preheat oven to 375.

items: In a large bowl combine the dry ingredients. In a separate bowl beat the eggs until frothy, then add the remaining wet ingredients. Add the wet ingredients to the dry and stir just enough to moisten. Too much mixing makes a tuff muffin. Fill lined muffin cups 3/4 full (I use a large icecream scoop) and bake for 20-25 minutes or until slightly golden.

All my recipes allow room for a little creative licence and a few corrective measures. So forget what momma always told you lol!

sections.text: Cream Cheese Icing (optional)

items: Toss all the room temperature ingredients into your mixer and whip until smooth.
Place a dollop of icing on the top of each muffin once they are completely cooled.

recipes.tip: This recipe is easily made gluten free by simply swapping out the flour with a gluten free version such as Robin Hood or my favourite flour blend. You can also make this vegan easily by using an egg replacer and garnishing with a dairy free icing.

recipes.title: Fire Roasted Tomato Soup
recipes.description: This quick and easy soup is very versatile...you can keep it as is or you can jazz it up a ton of different ways.

sections.text: Some good variations would be to add some chopped fresh herbs before serving...  parsley, basil and thyme work well. Why not stir in a spoon of pesto sauce and grate some parmesan cheese on top? Roasted garlic and chopped roasted red peppers are another nice addition, or even a simple dollop of creme fraiche and a sprinkle of fresh chopped dill. The possibilities are endless. If you thin the soup out a bit with some extra chicken stock you can always add some fresh seasonal vegetables such as green beans, potatoes, peas and corn, You could even add some beans or mini meatballs...your kids will love it, especially if they help make it!

items: 1 398ml can of diced fire roasted peppers

sections.text: salt and pepper to taste

items: Simply toss the first 3 ingredients into the blender and give it a whiz until smooth. Pour the tomato mixture into a medium sized pot on low heat. Now add the fire roasted peppers and give it a stir. Simmer on medium heat for about 10 -15 minutes or until it begins to boil. Lower the heat and stir in the heavy cream, season with salt and pepper. That's it, you're done. Enjoy!

recipes.tip: Vegan Option-  Simply swap out the cream with some coconut creamer.

recipes.title: MUFFIN OF THE MONTH- Coconut Matcha Latte MYFITNESSPAL.com
recipes.description: It's January and I've never been one to hop on the New Years resolution diet band wagon so yes, I  still have a MUFFIN OF THE MONTH in January lol.

sections.text: My resolutions lean more towards being and eating healthier. That to me means eating more nutrient dense foods, so this muffin fits the bill perfectly! They are rich and creamy just like a Matcha Latte thanks to the unusual addition of avocado...you read that right, avocado in a muffin! I figured why not include a healthy fat alternative that would amp up the gorgeous green colour. The Matcha green tea is full of antioxidants and fibre so these muffins will put a little spring in your step. Fantastic as a quick breakfast or a late afternoon snack. Best of all they take mere minutes to prepare. I make them so often I can do it with my eyes closed! I even sometimes prep the dry and wet ingredients the night before...stir them together in the morning and pop them in the oven to bake while I'm showering. Easy Peasy!
Preheat oven to 375.

items: In a large bowl combine the dry ingredients. In a separate bowl beat the eggs until frothy, then add the remaining wet ingredients. Add the wet ingredients to the dry and stir just enough to moisten. Too much mixing makes a tuff muffin. Fill lined muffin cups 3/4 full (I use a large icecream scoop) and bake for 20-25 minutes or until slightly golden.

*If for some reason your muffin mix seems a little dry and stiff feel free to stir in a splash more liquid. Conversley if it ends up a little wet, add a sprinkle more flour. recipes.title: Scented Play Dough

sections.text: I can think of no better way to get kids interested in cooking than teaching them how to make their own play dough. This recipe is particularly cool because it gets its color and scent from Kool- aide! I especially like homemade play dough because it’s slightly more moist so it's not as messy as the store bought stuff. It’s so cheap to make too...which is why this play dough recipe is a BEAUTIFUL THING!

items: 2tbs cream of tartar (really cheap in the bulk section!)

Mix all the ingredients together in a medium sized pot and cook over medium low heat until mixture becomes gummy. Let it cool a bit and then knead it like bread dough a few times so the colour becomes more consistent. Let it cool completely and store in an airtight container or a resealable plastic bag.

recipes.tip: The Play dough will be whatever color the Kool- aid crystals are.

recipes.title: Creamy Wild Mushroom Risotto
recipes.description: Well you know I'm feeling better when I feel like cooking again! YAY!!!!

sections.text: Unfortunately my jaw is still a bit sore from this awful bout of Shingles. So I figured what better way to ease myself back into eating solid food again than a nice creamy bowl of Risotto. This is on regular dinner rotation in our house...once you try it I'm sure it will be a favourite with your family too. My recipe is slightly different than most because it calls for a mix of water and stock. I do this because most people don't make their own stock these days and I find commercially prepared stock quite salty once its reduced, so this is my surefire way to get perfect risotto every time! Simply adjust the seasoning at the end after you've added the cheese.

items: This takes about 25 to 30 minutes to cook and should be served immediately.
3-4c wild mushrooms (if using dried soak in boiling water first)
2c water (or liquid from soaking dried mushrooms)

sections.text: Grated Parmesan or Asiago to taste (optional)
salt and pepper to taste

items: Slice your mushrooms and sauté them with the shallot in the olive oil and half of the butter over a medium heat in a large heavy bottomed pot. Once the shallots are fragrant and translucent add the wine or vermouth.
While the mushrooms are sautéing bring your stock and water to a boil in a separate pot. Once boiling turn to low and keep stock hot during the entire cooking process.
Toss the arborio rice into the pot with the mushrooms and shallot and give it a stir until the rice becomes slightly translucent. Keep the heat at medium-low.
Now simply ladle in some of the stock, and allow the rice to simmer until it has absorbed all the liquid, stirring regularly. Lots of stirring will help the risotto to become rich and creamy.
Continue adding stock a few ladles at a time, allowing the rice to fully absorb the liquid before adding any more. Be sure to stir every few minutes.

Once you've used all your stock, give the risotto a taste to make sure the rice is tender.  If its not you can add a bit of boing water the same way you did with the stock and continue cooking until tender. Once tender, stir in the rest of the butter, the cheese and the parsley and thyme.

sections.text: Season with salt and pepper to taste and serve immediately

recipes.title: Tropical Chia Pudding MYFITNESSPAL.com
recipes.description: Add a little sunshine to your day with this healthy little gem.

sections.text: It's easy to make and stores well for up to a week in the fridge so it's handy to have on hand as a healthy breakfast or a snack in a pinch. I like to use the empty glass jars from  petit pot yogurt, they even come with re-useable lids!

items: In a large bowl combine the first 6 ingredients. Divide into 8 single sized serving dishes. Now top each portion of chia pudding with some crushed pineapple and garnish with the toasted coconut. Cover and store in the fridge for up to 1 week.

recipes.title: Guilt Free Dark Chocolate Brownies
recipes.description: Okay, I'm not one for healthy desserts, desserts are supposed to be a treat so frankly I couldn't care less if they are healthy or not.

sections.text: My thought process though, has always been if you can make it healthier without affecting the flavour or texture why the heck wouldn't you?!!!!! This just so happens to be one of those recipes. It's quick and easy to make and tastes like every other fattening decadent brownie you've ever had. So enjoy your dessert with a little less guilt.

items: Simply mix the dry ingredients together in a large bowl. Now whisk the wet ingredients together in a separate bowl. Pour the wet ingredients over the dry and give a good stir until all the the dry ingredients are will incorporated...don't over mix.

Now simply pour the ingredients into a shallow parchment lined 9 X 9 baking pan. You can garnish the top with a few crushed nuts and some chocolate chips if you'd like. Bake for 25 minutes or until the brownie springs back when you gently press down on the centre.

recipes.title: Stinkbug Naturals
recipes.description: Stinkbug Naturals is a company I just discovered and I have to say I'm in love!

items: They have the coolest scents like Atomic, Floral Lime, Lavender, Vanilla Mint, Patchouli, Pine Cone, Tangerine Spice, Tea Tree and of course Unscented. They make one of the only Non-GMO Project Verified deodorants on the market and use "only organic ingredients that are free of aluminum and all other yucky toxins." For instance their main product is deodorant and it only contains: organic shea butter, organic beeswax, organic coconut oil, organic cornstarch, essential oils and baking soda. That's it! Nothing else, no strange words you can't pronounce, no artificial anything. Just pure natural ingredients you can trust. All of their products are made with organics are free of aluminums, paraben and are free of GMO ingredients. What more can you ask for? Oh yeah that's right they are made in the USA.

The product line is relatively small which is likely why the products are so AMAZING. So far my families favourite if I had to pick one would be the lip balm. It lasts incredibly long before you need to reapply it, and it's moisturizing without being sticky or gooey. They also carry hand sanitizers and as I mentioned deodorants. Both my daughters get terrible rashes from every deodorant they've ever used so I'm curious to see how this one is long term for them. I'll be sure to do an update in a couple of weeks to let you know, but so far so good...fingers crossed we may have finally found a winner.

Now for the hand sanitizers. They are alcohol free, smell so good you could almost use them as parfume and so far haven't irritated the severe eczema on my youngest daughters hands. Again I'll be sure to keep you posted as to how it is long term with her.
Okay I'll stop gushing about these products now...as you can see I'm totally enamoured with this company. In my books Stinkbug Naturals is a beautiful thing. Ihighly recommend you give them a try.

recipes.title: Cannéle De Bordeaux
recipes.description: Many of you have likely not heard of this little french treasure. I know I hadn't until visiting Paris for the first time and I've been hooked ever since!

sections.text: I'm so in love with these that every time I  go to Paris I'm on a mission to find the best ones, I'll stop in 4 or 5 pâtisseries a day just looking for them...my husband thinks I'm nuts.

items: A Cannéle is French pastry flavoured with rum and vanilla. It has a soft and tender custard center and a dark, thick caramelized crust. Originally a specialty of the Bordeaux region of France, today it is widely available in pâtisseries all over France and, as I've now happily discovered, if you look hard enough you may be lucky enough to find them abroad.

sections.text: Cannéle are traditionally baked in the prettiest little cylindrical fluted copper molds. There are molds available made of silicone but I personally think the crust wouldn't be of the same quality baked in a silicone mold. Traditionally the moulds are brushed with beeswax, but today butter is often used instead. I've also noticed that the amount of rum used varies greatly from pâtisserie to pâtisserie. At times the rum is very subtle and other times it's so strong I'd be scared to drive after eating one for fear I'd be over the legal limit lol.

items: Now you may be wondering why I'm not attempting to make these myself. Well, my answer is twofold. First the traditional copper molds used to make them are prohibitively expensive... they start at 20 euros each! It would be silly to make a batch smaller than 12 so not only would the molds cost me a small fortune, but I also have absolutely no self control so I likely would eat the entire batch myself lol. I'm much better off purchasing 4 at a time and thanks to Trader Joe's I can actually do that now. The package says to microwave them but I would recommend baking them in a 350 degree oven for 10 minutes or until they become rich and dark. Let cool completely before eating. Let me know what you think?!!!! I think cannéles are a beautiful thing.
